title: Concrete Pump Priming and Line Lubrication (Grout, Not Water)
seoTitle: Concrete Pump Priming and Grout Lubrication | Pinjin Xingtai
description: ACPA says always prime the pump and placing line before concrete; a thin Portland-cement slurry is the preferred primer, and water priming is not recommended in most cases. Pinjin does not publish a factory primer recipe. Match the trailer row, then inquire.

relatedPaths.label: Concrete pump blockage causes and safe response

answerBlock.what: ACI 304.2R: pumped concrete rides on a thin lubricating film on the pipe wall; coat the entire interior diameter with grout or a specialised primer before concrete. ACPA (23 July 2020): always prime the pump and placing line; the optimal primer is a thin Portland-cement slurry; in most cases ACPA does not recommend water priming. Pinjin does not print a sack count or factory primer mix. Wetting the hopper is not line lubrication.
answerBlock.who: Operators starting a trailer pipeline pour who will use a listed Pinjin pump and a steel or hose line assembled on site.
factors: Prime the pump and the placing line before the first concrete
Prefer a thin Portland-cement slurry, not water, unless ACPA’s later graphic says otherwise for that method
Keep the mix consistent once flow is established so the film is maintained
Pinjin does not publish a primer recipe or guaranteed first-load cubic metres

faqs.question: Can I prime a Pinjin trailer pump with water instead of grout?
faqs.answer: ACPA revised its water-priming statement: always prime the pump and placing line before concrete; the preferred primer is a thin Portland-cement slurry. In most cases ACPA does not recommend water priming. Pinjin does not publish a factory primer recipe or sack count. Do not treat ‘wet the hopper’ as a substitute for line lubrication.

faqs.question: Does the catalogue list how many cement sacks to prime Electric 40?
faqs.answer: No. Electric 40 lists 45 kW, 21 m³/h, 23 MPa, hopper 0.4 m³ and fine-stone 120 m / 360 m. Primer volume is not a catalogue cell. ACPA: use the methods that coat 100 percent of the pipe wall. Send pipe length and DN with the model slug if you want Xingtai to comment on a listed trailer, not on an unpublished recipe.

faqs.question: Does priming replace a daily hopper and grate check?
faqs.answer: No. Priming coats the line. The Xingtai daily checklist still starts at the hopper and grate, then clamps, leaks and S-valve observation. See the maintenance checklist. A dirty grate that drops oversize stone into the valve is a blockage cause, not a priming shortcut.
